kind: simulated (generated trip telemetry and fuel; a method check, not a measured fleet)
question: Can trip telemetry flag fuel-inefficient trips, and predict litres per 100 km, better than a fleet-average rule?

data.label: actual L/100 km > 1.15 x reference (class/payload base term only)
data.excess_fuel: litres above the reference; includes condition effects (cold, stops, speed) as well as driving

class_mean.inputs: vehicle class only (training mean L/100 km per class)

fleet_average_rule.inputs: the trip's MEASURED L/100 km against 1.15 x the training class median; ignores payload

fleet_average_rule_f1_tuned.inputs: same score as fleet_average_rule; its line moved to maximise F1 on validation (threshold parity with the models)

class_share.inputs: vehicle class only (training inefficient share per class)

models.threshold_rule: classifier thresholds maximise F1 on the validation months; the fleet-average rule uses its own fixed 1.15 x median line
models.tuning: ridge and logistic L2 penalty from [0.01, 0.1, 1.0, 10.0, 100.0, 1000.0] on validation (MAE / log-loss); LightGBM early stopping (100 rounds) on validation; all fitted on training months only

assumptions: base rates (L/100 km empty and full) per class are ASSUMED round numbers: {"van": [8.5, 11.5], "rigid": [20.0, 28.0], "articulated": [24.0, 36.0]}

effect sizes on fuel (idle, harsh acceleration, speed, stops, temperature, age) are ASSUMED: {"idle_per_share": 0.5, "idle_typical": 0.1, "harsh_per_event": 0.01, "harsh_typical": 4.0, "speed_quadratic": 0.0001, "speed_best_kmh": 65.0, "stops_per_stop": 0.03, "cold_per_c": 0.006, "cold_below_c": 10.0, "heat_per_c": 0.004, "heat_above_c": 25.0, "age_per_year": 0.008, "age_typical": 6.0}
20 % of drivers carry a hidden +0.09 fuel share no telemetry field records (ASSUMED), plus more idling and harsh acceleration
trip noise on the fuel multiplier Normal(0, 0.05) (ASSUMED)
CO2 factor 2.5 kg CO2 per litre of diesel is ASSUMED (rounded); check the current official conversion factor before external use
temperate seasonal temperature cycle (4 C January to 18 C July) plus Normal(0, 3.5) weather noise (ASSUMED)
limits: the trips are generated: the models can only recover effects that were put in, and their accuracy reflects the chosen noise level
no real telematics or fuel-card data; replace generate() with recorded trips and fuel readings
the CO2 factor is assumed, so the CO2 figures are fuel litres times an assumed constant
the telemetry models do not see the trip's fuel reading while the fleet-average rule does: different information, stated per model
'inefficient' is measured against the class/payload base term, so cold weather and stop-heavy routes count as excess alongside driving behaviour
one simulated fleet, one seed, one chronological split (test = months 11-12, colder than most of the training year)
the label counts trips (ratio to reference) while the excess-captured share weights by litres, so long heavy trips dominate it and the two can rank models differently
